summary: instagram-bridge: GET /accounts?username= resolves a handle to at most one account, filtered to an exact, case-insensitive match.
details: New resource GET /accounts?username= (design/instagram-adoption/16 §Resources, 17 P9, P10) over the same instameow search port GET /accounts?query= already uses. P9 measured that the search finds accounts beyond Nora's DM contacts, private ones included, but that one exact match was not the first result — so this route filters the raw hits to an exact, case-insensitive username equality in the app layer (app.LookupAccountByUsername) and never takes items[0].

The 200 body is the SAME list shape ?query= answers: {items:[...], next_cursor:null}, with 0 or 1 items. Zero matches is a normal empty list, not a 404 — the mechanism cannot tell 'no such account' from 'the search missed it'. Two or more exact matches cannot happen for a real username (they are unique), so it is 502 upstream_rejected.

username follows Instagram's own handle alphabet ([A-Za-z0-9._]{1,30}), with one leading @ stripped; anything else is 400 before the session gate. username together with query, or either repeated, is also 400.

The username never enters a span attribute, event, name, status, log line, or the error envelope's message — domain.ParseUsername's own error text embeds the raw input, so this route answers a fixed message instead of forwarding it.
limitations: Nora's Python side is untouched: profile and story links are not wired to this route yet (17 P10's Nora half — instagram_links.py, the router, and the negative/multi-account tests).
